newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil ends week higher.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil ends week higher.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run prices ended the week higher on the offer side on the back of recent gains in crude and increasing demand, traders said.

A refiner was heard to have moved a cargo of 0.5 pct sulphur material but the deal could not be immediately confirmed. The seller was heard offering at $109 fob, or a few dollars higher than earlier levels this week.
"The market has two fundamental reasons to go up. Crude prices are higher and the supply/demand differential is giving the market a push," a trader with a refiner said.
"There are some people who are desperate for prompt barrels now," a trader with a refiner said.
With most of the July material gone, with the exception of a 20,000-tonne piece being re-offered by a U.S. independent refiner, talk is concentrating on August barrels.
Russian M-100 high sulphur straight-run was said to have traded at two means plus $5 or a little higher late on Thursday, a price said to be reflective of the market.
